question:
A 33-year-old woman reports experiencing vulvar pain, itching, dysuria, and urethral discharge for the
past three days. Her symptoms are accompanied by fever, malaise, myalgias, and headaches. She
describes severe pain during urination, leading her to avoid using the toilet. She recently returned from
a tropical vacation, during which she engaged in multiple unprotected sexual encounters with both men
and women. Her vital signs include a temperature of 38.7°C (101.6°F), heart rate of 90/min, and
respiratory rate of 17/min. On pelvic examination, there are vulvar ulcers and excoriations without
vesicles, as well as erythema and edema of the vaginal mucosa, but no purulent discharge. Which test
or characteristic is most effective in identifying the subtype of the causative organism? Answer
Choices: (A) Tzanck smear (B) Culture in Thayer-Martin agar (C) Serology (D) Nucleic acid
amplification test (NAAT) (E) Dark-field microscopy (F) PCR amplification of viral DNA (G) Direct
fluorescence antigen (DFA) (H) Viral culture with typing (I) Western blot analysis (J) Gram stain of
urethral discharge
 A. Direct fluorescence antigen (DFA)
B. Dark-field microscopy
C. Viral culture with typing
D. Tzanck smear
E. PCR amplification of viral DNA
F. Western blot analysis
G. Nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT)
H. Culture in Thayer-Martin agar
I. Gram stain of urethral discharge
J. Serology
